messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in 5xxs from EU edge cluster and automatic fallback events detected (smart-routing). error_rate_eu increased to 12% in the last 5m. possible routing loop. Paging oncall. :rotating_light:
pagerduty: Page sent to @sre-alex (on-call) — Sev2. See incident thread.
anya: saw this on dashboard. EU backend suddenly started returning 502s and then traffic jumped to US-west via fallback. customers in eu-west report degraded responses.
matt: i ran a quick dig against the authoritative set. looks like several geo rrset entries for eu.example.edge.redwood.ai are stale — TTLs expired but registrar propagation inconsistent.
	snippet:
	```
	$ dig +short eu.example.edge.redwood.ai
	192.0.2.10
	198.51.100.23  # old endpoint that should have been removed
	```
	same in multiple locations, some resolvers still returning old IP.
sre-alex: on it. currently checking smart-routing policy evaluation logs to see why fallback kicked in (shouldn’t cross-region for latency SLOs). taking traffic-snapshot.
eng-runtime: looking at policy engine logs — we see a cascade: health check flapping for eu-primary pool, policy matched fallback: allow-cross-region=true for tier=free and no pinned-model tag. That allowed US fallback, but the US endpoints returned a different model variant (v1-quantized) causing internal validation errors in the runtime -> 502s -> health probes fail -> further fallback attempts => loop.
anya: oh — that explains customer reports about "wrong completions" then 5xxs. Product tag mismatch maybe.
support-jules: opened CS ticket #INC-9134, impacted customers: acme-charts (EU users), beta-retail (EU), ~12 total orgs. Notified CSMs.
product-sam: need a short message for status page: impacted EU traffic, fallback loop causing intermittent errors and wrong-model responses. ETA unknown.
matt: quick mitigation idea: disable cross-region fallback policy temporarily and pin EU hostnames to eu-primary IPs via traffic manager (bypass smart-routing). Will need to update routing config and then perform a controlled failover.
infra-lee: we can set a route override in traffic-manager to force eu.example.edge.redwood.ai -> 192.0.2.11 (known-good eu endpoint) and disable geo-fallback. Doing that now will avoid DNS cache issues because resolver will hit override at our edge/proxy layer.
sre-alex: agree. apply override and then re-evaluate health checks. also reduce health-check sensitivity (increase consecutive failures required) to avoid flip-flop during verification.
deploy-bot: deploy triggered: traffic-manager override patch by infra-lee in prod (rollout id: rtm-2026-453).
infra-lee: patch applied, stepping to 50% for eu edge proxies. monitoring logs.
eng-runtime: logs show errors falling to baseline in EU after override. cross-region fallback count dropped to 0 in last 2m.
anya: support_jules — please confirm any customer-facing messages we should push.
support-jules: posting to status page now: short note — "We are investigating intermittent errors for EU customers caused by routing/fallback interactions. Mitigation in progress." link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1850002222
product-sam: question: how did wrong model variant end up on US fallback endpoints? is this a release tagging issue or runtime selector mismatch?
eng-runtime: preliminary: model variant labeling mismatch during a recent rollout. The selector expression for fallback-compatible models used label "compatible_with_fallback: true" — one canary variant was missing that label but still reported capacity, and a separate automation retrofitted the label incorrectly on the US pool, causing an incompatible quantized variant to be served.
sre-alex: for postmortem we should capture: (1) DNS propagation stale rrsets -> caused resolvers to hit removed endpoints, (2) policy allow-cross-region enabled fallback which was a safety hole, (3) model-label mismatch allowed incompatible model in fallback pool, (4) health-check thresholds too aggressive, creating oscillation.
anya: immediate next steps?
sre-alex: 1) keep traffic override until authority DNS is cleaned and we’ve observed stable health for 30m. 2) rollback the label change or restrict fallback candidate pool to explicitly whitelisted model-ids. 3) add a policy hard-stop: do not allow cross-region fallback if model_variant != primary_variant. 4) contact registrar/authoritative DNS team to purge stale rrsets and lower TTLs for a controlled window.
infra-lee: started DNS change request to remove deprecated rrsets and set TTL=60 for edge records. Est propagation ~5-15m after update depending on external caches. Request ID: DNS-REQ-2026-78.
pagerduty: @sre-alex acknowledged the page. Estimated time on scene: 35m.
eng-runtime: quick config snippet to patch policy (pseudocode):
	```
	policy.fallback:
	  allow_cross_region: false  # temp
	  require_variant_match: true
	  whitelisted_variants: ["v1-onnx", "v1-int8"]
	```
product-sam: notify sales for customers with active SLAs. We need to offer a detailed post-incident summary.
support-jules: CS pinged, all impacted customers informed with interim mitigation and expected timeline.
matt: monitoring shows resolver-level variance — some EU resolvers still returning old IP for up to ~40s after our override, but hit rate is dropping.
sre-alex: starting handoff in 20m to night oncall. will assemble runbook and write initial timeline.
anya: can you include a list of queries and how we confirmed model mismatch?
sre-alex: added diagnostic steps to the runbook: curl header checks to validate model id in response: `x-model-id` header, runtime logs filtered by request ids. Also saved sample request/response pairs to artifacts bucket: s3://redwood-incidents/1850002222/artifacts (access: incident-team).
eng-runtime: we should add an automated test to the pre-rollout checklist: verify fallback pool responds with matching `x-model-id`.
product-sam: agreed. Also create a QA gate to block label changes from being applied via automation without a manual approval for production tag changes.
deploy-bot: rollback of the faulty model-label patch scheduled in 10m if not acknowledged.
infra-lee: DNS authority update completed; TTL set to 60. Monitoring external resolver responses.
matt: external dig shows most resolvers now returning only correct IPs.
anya: status update for channel: mitigation in place — traffic override + policy tightened. Impacted customers notified. Oncall to monitor; next update in 30m or on重大 change. :thumbsup:
sre-alex: note for handoff: current state — override still active, cross-region fallback disabled, model-label rollback in progress, DNS cleaned. Error rate EU down to 1.6%, latency stable. Handoff to night-oncall at 1850008400.
product-sam: thanks all. postmortem owner: eng-runtime / sre team. please start collecting timeline and RCA items.
support-jules: updating incident ticket and CS notes.
incident-bot: Incident 1850002222 status: Mitigated (partial) — monitoring. Severity downgraded to P2.
anya: closing thread for now but keep watch. will reopen if regression.
